title: Proposed common4 with explicit history and new-Plan recognition details
description: Evaluator3 output profile. Product output identities are run3, evidence3, finding3, subject3. Native/input identities remain snapshot2, plan2, closure2, import2, fact2, coverage2, view2, exec-plan2, finding-key2. This profile MUST NOT admit mixed output-major prefixes (no run2/run3 alternation). Fingerprint correspondence remains finding-key2. ScopeDocumentV1 and WaiverSetV1 stay on the original policy-document owner. Isolated successor; not a rewrite of frozen workflow1. Joint source succession uses a distinct common4 schema identifier; historical common3 and every historical carrier retain their pinned vocabulary.

ExecutionId.description: EXECUTION-ID-V1: exact selector docs/coop/artifacts/c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json $.planIntent.wireTypes.executionId (grammar only; that artifact records under ownershipHonesty/RES-C2V4-01 that no producing recipe is declared anywhere in the corpus). Production values are host-minted 128-bit operational identifiers of the same shape as REQUEST-ID-V1; they are never derived from content. The reference model's values are SYNTHETIC fixture labels (see workflows_model.synthetic_execution_id) and are not a recipe. The historical R-1 fixture grammar 'execution:<text>' is not admitted by this unit.

LogicalPath.description: Strict sealed logical path: relative, slash-separated, no empty/dot/dot-dot/NUL/backslash segments, each segment at most 255 bytes-as-characters. Used for snapshot inventories, edits, archive members, cwd and every identity-bearing path. Never a user-typed OS path.

UserInputPath.description: A user-named OS path (baseline file, import artifact, output file). Opened only through the security unit's nofollow/ACL custody; never enters any content identity; recorded in operational records only.

GlobPattern.description: Portable glob matching is normative in docs/coop/design-corrections/foundation/glob-pattern-contract.v1.md: full-string, case-sensitive matching; '*' and '?' stay within a segment; whole-segment '**' matches zero or more segments including a final filename. Braces and brackets are literal; no escape syntax. Candidate admission remains owned by its field.

D9FaultCause.description: Which operational fault applies. `host-invariant` is the successor member and its scope is narrow: the closed D9ErrorCode vocabulary already published SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE with no cause mapping to it, so the host-INVARIANT subtype specifically had no representable operational-failed termination, because that class requires BOTH an errorCode and a non-none faultCause. Other host-fault causes - host-io, ledger-corrupt, provider-protocol and the rest - already existed and were always representable. PRECISION: codeMaps.rule's `total and injective` is a property of the DECLARED CAUSE DOMAIN, so an errorCode without a preimage was never a violation of totality, and this member does not `make the maps total`. It adds no error code, class, exit code or reason code, but it IS a vocabulary extension: faultCause grows by one. The inherited docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json is HISTORICAL and unchanged, so its own enum still omits the member; the selected composition is native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-public-route-registry/hostInvariantSuccessor and publishing the successor D9 artifact belongs to that unit. Borrowing host-io for a host invariant violation is refused by contract: an I/O failure and an invariant violation are different remedies.

D9Deficiency.description: The HOST TERMINATION deficiency vocabulary of the D9 exit contract, carried by a whole Run, analysis result or comparison step: AnalysisResult.deficiency / .secondaryDeficiencies, ComparisonStepResult.d9Deficiency and comparison-result. It is NOT the per-requirement native sufficiency vocabulary, and the two are deliberately different sets. Three members (convergence-exhausted, baseline-recipe-unsupported, query-completeness-unmet) belong to evaluation, baseline and query outcomes that no per-requirement sufficiency evaluation can produce; `none` is the whole-Run `nothing was deficient` state, which a per-requirement record expresses by satisfied=true and the absence of the field. Four native sufficiency outcomes (derivation-policy-unmet, external-consumers-unknown, input-closure-incomplete, resolution-incomplete) have NO member here at all: they project outward as their own DomainDetailCode members and as the D9 class `indeterminate` (3) with the existing error code, per native-evidence.md section 10. Widening this enum to carry them was refused: it would put per-requirement causes into a whole-Run vocabulary and would change the D9 exit contract. Use #/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency wherever the value is one requirement's own outcome. PROVENANCE: this ENUM is unchanged from the inherited D9 exit contract and no member was added, removed or reordered by any correction in this series. The DEFINITION BYTES of this $defs entry did change, because this description was added; an earlier handoff said the definition was byte-unchanged, which was true only of the enum.

ImportedRequirementDeficiency.description: The IMPORTED-EVIDENCE per-requirement outcome vocabulary, owned by imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law. It applies to a repair EvidenceRequirement whose relation is `runtime-observation` or `history-change` - relations that mint no fact2, carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse and have no Coverage entry, so native section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2` cannot produce an outcome for them and is not asked to. Every member is bound to the payload field that grounds it, and EACH KIND REPORTS ONLY ITS OWN: a runtime requirement is projected through observability, observationWindow and observedPopulation; a history requirement through revisionRange and collectionScope, which are its BOUNDS fields - HistoryPayloadV1 has others, notably its subjects, but it carries no observationWindow, observedPopulation or observability at all. A satisfied imported requirement means the condition was met over the BOUND window or range - not that the evidence is positive: `observed-hit` is positive execution evidence and `observable-unhit` is bounded NEGATIVE evidence, and the disclosure records which satisfied it. No imported observation establishes a universal negative, and imported evidence can never BY ITSELF establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe delete or replace - though it may be an additional required condition alongside an already-established native basis.

x-opensip-vocabulary.admittedBy: workflows_model.admit_evidence_requirement, which decides the plane from the relation registry before reading the value
x-opensip-vocabulary.note: GENERATED/DRIFT-CHECKED from the law's outcome keys in its declared precedence order. It is a DIFFERENT vocabulary from NativeSufficiencyDeficiency and the two never mix: a native requirement carrying an imported outcome, or the reverse, is refused.

NativeSufficiencyDeficiency.description: The NATIVE PER-REQUIREMENT sufficiency outcome vocabulary: the exact nine members of DeficiencyV2, whose only defined producer is native-evidence.md section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2`, evaluated once per requirement. A record carrying one requirement's own outcome carries THIS vocabulary and never D9Deficiency, because four of these nine members have no D9Deficiency preimage and the D9-mapped value for all four is the same `verdict-indeterminate`, which would collapse exactly the distinction native-evidence.md section 10 preserves per row - including `resolution-incomplete`, the outcome section 4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal negative under unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid over an affected target, and the outcome a destructive unused-code repair recipe turns on. This record-level vocabulary is orthogonal to two other things and replaces neither: the PUBLIC D9 TERMINATION of the Run that carries the requirement (still #/$defs/D9Deficiency and the section 10 class/code columns), and the retained CAUSE CARRIER of the Coverage entry the outcome was read from (still entry.nativeCause or the named structured carrier, per the native deficiency-cause registry). `none` is deliberately absent: a satisfied requirement is satisfied=true with the field omitted, which is what sufficiency_v2 returns.

x-opensip-vocabulary.admittedBy: workflows_model.admit_evidence_requirement at the repair-preview producer/consumer boundary; enum parity re-checked cross-unit by check-integration.py
x-opensip-vocabulary.note: GENERATED/DRIFT-CHECKED: this enum is exactly DeficiencyV2 in DeficiencyV2's own declared member order, mirrored here because the workflows schema bundle resolves only urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:* references and takes no cross-bundle $ref. It is the same closed vocabulary, not a workflows-owned successor: a member added or removed on either side is a drift failure, never a widening of this one.

DomainDetailCode.description: Generated/drift-checked from docs/coop/design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json plus isolated evaluator3 members. Every owner joins the same closed registry; unknown names refuse. These details do not create D9 codes. Isolated additions: BASELINE.ENTRY_PROJECTION_CONFLICT, COMPARISON.CORRESPONDENCE_INCOMPLETE, EVALUATION.FINDING_JOIN_REFUSED, EVALUATION.MIXED_OUTPUT_MAJOR, EVALUATION.OUTPUT_BOUND_EXCEEDED, EVALUATION.PROOF_VERDICT_INCONSISTENT, EVALUATION.PROJECTION_INPUT_INCOMPLETE, EVALUATION.WORK_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, QUERY.CURSOR_MISMATCH, QUERY.ENDPOINT_AMBIGUOUS, QUERY.ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN, QUERY.FACT_VIEW_UNAVAILABLE, QUERY.PARAMS_MALFORMED, QUERY.RELATION_UNSUPPORTED, QUERY.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED, QUERY.VIEW_AMBIGUOUS, QUERY.VIEW_UNKNOWN, REPAIR.TARGET_CORRESPONDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, REPAIR.TARGET_METADATA_AMBIGUOUS. Shared registry members this surface must preserve (root registers in both common enums): EVALUATION.INPUT_REFUSED (structural evaluator input failure with the exact diagnostic retained separately), EVALUATION.SELECTION_LIMIT (well-formed prospective request above the published bound), EVALUATION.REQUIRED_OUTPUT_OMITTED (missing required provider or host output pointer on the public surface, retaining its exact reference). Do not fork a second registration. CONFIG.INVALID is a D9ErrorCode and a DomainDetailCode; it is not an arbitrary DomainDetail for evaluator3 join/projection refusals. Root integrates. Output bound error is existing D9ErrorCode OUTPUT.SERIALIZATION_FAILED with faultCause output-serialization, never HOST.IO_FAILURE.

code.description: This typed record declares exactly one condition - a capability the selected product requires that this release did not declare available - so its code is that condition, not any DomainDetailCode. An earlier revision referenced the whole enum and admitted CONFIG.INVALID on a release-absence notice.

CapabilityAvailabilityNoticeV1.description: One capability the selected product requires that this release did not declare available, for ONE requested unit. The ownership tuple is carried in TYPED FIELDS - capabilityId, languageMode and the unit's own workspaceRoot - and is never concatenated into `subject`: workspaceRoot is a UserInputPath bounded at 4096 while BoundedText is 1024, so a concatenated subject could silently truncate a path and collapse two distinct requested units into one indistinguishable notice. Advisory: it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control verdict or repair authority, and is never a clone Candidate.

CapabilityAvailabilityV1.description: The invocation's availability account, composed PER STEP. An earlier revision used one flat array bounded at 1024 and argued it could not truncate because that is the analysis-spec bound - but 1024 is per analysis-spec, not per invocation, and a named multi-step invocation carries up to 64 steps: two admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices and the flat array refused. Composing per step preserves every valid admitted invocation: each step keeps its own bounded collection, `steps` is bounded by the invocation step bound (StepId 0..63), and no notice is ever discarded to fit. `totalNoticeCount` is the sum of the step counts and is authoritative for a caller counting absences across the invocation. A step that made no selection - a skipped step, or a non-analysis step - contributes NO entry; a step that selected and found nothing absent contributes an entry with an empty array, which is the positive statement that it checked. A retried step keeps ONE entry, for the attempt whose selection the invocation retained.

StepTermination.description: D9-shaped per-step or aggregate termination. exitCode is never stored; it derives from class by the fixed table (0,1,2,3,4,130). Branch contract: success carries no errorCode/reasonCodes/signal; policy-failed requires runId, or authority=ephemeral when the failing analysis was explicitly non-authoritative and therefore has no Run; request-rejected and operational-failed require errorCode (operational-failed also a non-none faultCause); indeterminate requires reasonCodes; interrupted requires signal and may carry runId only when a Run was committed before the interrupt. Retained D9 class/code legality (X1, X3, X4 and codeDerivation) is schema-enforced on the same branches: faultCause appears only on operational-failed and pairs with errorCode exactly as the fault map (D9 codeMaps.faultCauseToErrorCode plus the successor host-invariant member); reasonCodes appear only on indeterminate. Required-delivery detail law: DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT names a failure after this invocation committed a Run and requires that runId; DELIVERY.REQUIRED_PROJECTION_FAILED names a required projection or renderer failure when no Run was committed and forbids runId. Both are operational-failed / DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED; every other operational-failed termination keeps its existing optional runId.

SourceCorrespondence.description: Mandatory correspondence of external evidence to analyzed source. exact-snapshot binds a snapshot2 and is the only correspondence that is mapped by itself. vcs-revision binds a commit plus dirty flag and optional build identity; a commit string (even clean) or a declared build identity is a STATEMENT and cannot prove which generated/runtime bytes correspond to which snapshot bytes, so vcs-revision evidence is consumable only when an admitted SourceMappingV1 (imported-evidence schema) joins every consumed generated path to a snapshot2 inventory entry by digest; otherwise it is unmapped-only. The wrapper's sourceCorrespondenceDigest is the raw SHA-256 of this record's canonical bytes, retained as a blob.

sourceMappingDigest.description: raw SHA-256 of the canonical SourceMappingV1 bytes admitted with this evidence, or null when none was supplied (then vcs-revision evidence is unmapped-only)

RepairAuthorizationRef.description: Exact product H(security.repair-apply-authorization.v1, admitted RepairApplyAuthorizationV1) with the security.repair-apply-authorization.v1 prefix; current host admission is mandatory.

PinnedPurgeDisclosure.description: Complete current pin inventory observed under the purge writer lease. Operational pinId is a host-ledger name scoped to this Run, not a content identity or authority token. Never truncate this disclosure or infer destructive consent from it.

CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1.description: The availability account of ONE analysis step's own selection, associated with that step by stepId. `notices` is bounded at 1024 because that is the analysis-spec requestedCapabilities bound and one selection produces at most one absence per requested row, so a STEP's collection can never truncate and its noticeCount always equals its array length. The same ownership tuple may recur in different steps - two steps may select the same unit - so uniqueness is within a step, never across the invocation.

FindingId.description: Evaluator3 finding identity. Not a fingerprint. Duplicate fingerprints across configurations are normal; maps key by this id.

SubjectId.description: Opaque subject3 identity. Workflow projection must not unpack universe/kind/nativeId. Path for waiver, baseline subjectPath and repair metadata is finding.subject.logicalPath. For packages that path is the package manifest path (package names may repeat).

NullableFingerprint.description: Matched findings carry finding-key2. Unmatched findings MUST be JSON null, never a surrogate or a run2/finding2 prefix.

UnmatchedOccurrence.description: Retained unmatched finding metadata. Excluded from fingerprint-keyed baseline entries. side is baseline or current. Historical schemaMajor 1 artifacts do not acquire an empty array assertion.

partialFingerprints.description: SARIF stable partialFingerprints. Present only for matched findings.

FindingSurface.description: Intermediate host finding projection, not a SARIF 2.1 result. One row per finding3. The SARIF adapter is urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:evaluator3:sarif-adapter:2.

gating.description: Derived from admitted PolicyDocumentV2 enabled AND gate AND severity floor. Never inferred from ruleResults.outcome.

CorrespondenceCoverage.description: Per-rule correspondence coverage, including zero-finding rules. populationUnknown is semantic incomplete (unavailable inventory record or no-covering-program), not a fabricated unavailable outcome for a missing expected inventory pointer (that pointer absence is structural refusal owned by enumeration/composition admission).

x-opensip-output-profile.note: Patterns are exact single-major. Broad run[23] regex is forbidden.
